process_area.title: Apprenticeship Cohort Operations, Mentorship & Competency Assessment

value_stream.name: Skilled-Trade Apprenticeship, Vocational Education & Capability Pipeline

fields.Participants: Trade Capability, L&D (links to VS-19.4), Store Ops (links to VS-07), DC Ops (links to VS-04), HR (links to VS-19), Finance (links to VS-17.4), In-Store Services (links to VS-09)

workflows.name: Apprenticeship Cohort Planning, Scheduling & Resource Allocation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "schedule, store/DC rotation slots, and instructor/mentor capacity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-allocate of "allocate apprentices to stores/DCs balancing learning value, store capacity,…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "Trade Capability/Finance allocate program resources" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-599 (ensure controlled execution — Apprenticeship Cohort Operations, Mentorship & Competency Assessment (PA-123.2).)
- operational: capacity planning; operational: rotation scheduling
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capacity-mismatch risk**: Too many apprentices for store/mentor capacity; mitigated by capacity planning
- **Rotation-gap risk**: Apprentice stuck in one department; mitigated by rotation scheduling
System Touchpoints: - L&D (links to VS-19.4); workforce planning (links to VS-103.3); store ops (links to VS-07); DC (links to VS-04); finance (links to VS-17.4); PPE (links to W172)

steps.activity: Trade Capability/L&D plan cohorts: cohort size/intake aligned to capability needs and store-growth (links to VS-37/VS-103.3), intake calendar, theory/practical schedule, store/DC rotation slots, and instructor/mentor capacity (links to W3820)

Trade Capability/Store-Ops allocate apprentices to stores/DCs balancing learning value, store capacity, trade coverage, and regional distribution, and schedule rotation across departments (lumber, tiles, plumbing, electrical, paint, tools)
steps.r: Trade Capability / Store Ops / DC Ops

steps.activity: Trade Capability/Finance allocate program resources: instructors, materials, tools/PPE kits (links to W172/W3823), facilities, and budget tracking (links to W3812)

fields.Participants: Trade Capability, Store Ops (links to VS-07), Master Tradespersons/Mentors (links to W3820), In-Store Services (links to VS-09), L&D (links to VS-19.4), HSE (links to VS-24)

workflows.name: Apprentice On-the-Job Training, Rotation & Store Assignment Operations

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "log competencies practiced and signed off against the curriculum" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-599 (ensure controlled execution — Apprenticeship Cohort Operations, Mentorship & Competency Assessment (PA-123.2).)
- operational: mentor sign-off required on each competency unit; on-the-job hours logged and auditable against TESDA requirements
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-supervision risk**: Apprentice given unsafe/unsupervised tasks; mitigated by mentor supervision
- **Service-disruption risk**: Apprentice activity disrupts store service; mitigated by integration standards
System Touchpoints: - Store ops (links to VS-07); in-store services (links to VS-09); L&D/competency (links to VS-19.4); HSE (links to VS-24); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Trade Capability/Store-Ops execute on-the-job training: department rotation, supervised practice at the lumber yard, tile gallery, plumbing/electrical, paint-tinting station, tools wall, and fabrication/estimation bay (links to VS-09.1/VS-09.2), under mentor supervision (links to W3820)

Trade Capability/Mentors log competencies practiced and signed off against the curriculum (links to W3810/W3815), capturing evidence (work samples, supervisor sign-off) for assessment (links to W3819)

Trade Capability/Store-Ops integrate apprentices into store operations safely and productively (age/role-appropriate tasks, supervision, customer interaction standards) without compromising service (links to VS-07) or safety (links to W3823)

fields.Participants: Trade Capability, Master Tradespersons/Assessors (links to W3828), L&D (links to VS-19.4/W683), Compliance (links to VS-22), Quality (links to VS-31), TESDA (links to W3811)

workflows.name: Trade Competency Assessment, Practical Examination & Certification Sign-Off

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-measure of "measure lumber board-foot, lay a tile sample, fit a pipe joint, tint a paint…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "center standards, and capture results/certification" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-issue of "issue BuildRight internal trade certification and TESDA certification" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standards and assessor qualification (links to W3828); operational: remediation pathway
Pain Points / Risks: - **Assessment-inconsistency risk**: Different assessors grade differently; mitigated by standards and assessor qualification (links to W3828)
- **Certification-blockage risk**: Apprentice stuck without certification; mitigated by remediation pathway
System Touchpoints: - L&D/competency (links to VS-19.4/W683); compliance (links to VS-22); quality (links to VS-31); records (links to VS-88); TESDA (links to W3811)

steps.activity: Trade Capability/Master-Tradespersons run competency assessments per the curriculum (links to W3810): written/theory, practical demonstration (e.g., cut-and-measure lumber board-foot, lay a tile sample, fit a pipe joint, tint a paint sample, safe power-tool operation), and structured scoring

Trade Capability/Compliance coordinate TESDA NC/COC assessment where applicable (links to W3811), ensure assessor qualification and assessment-center standards, and capture results/certification (links to W3815)

Trade Capability issue BuildRight internal trade certification and TESDA certification (links to W3815), manage re-assessment/remediation for not-yet-competent apprentices (links to W3821), and feed results into placement (links to W3822)

fields.Participants: Trade Capability, Store Ops (links to VS-07), Master Tradespersons, L&D (links to VS-19.4), HR (links to VS-102/VS-103), Recognition (links to W630)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify and qualify master tradespersons per trade/store, define mentor role…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "Trade Capability manage mentor–apprentice matching, coaching cadence, and mentor" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-599 (ensure controlled execution — Apprenticeship Cohort Operations, Mentorship & Competency Assessment (PA-123.2).)
- operational: mentor development (links to W3828); operational: capacity management and recognition
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mentor-shortage risk**: Not enough qualified mentors; mitigated by mentor development (links to W3828)
- **Mentor-burnout risk**: Mentors overloaded; mitigated by capacity management and recognition
System Touchpoints: - Store ops (links to VS-07); L&D (links to VS-19.4); recognition (links to W630); compensation (links to VS-102); HR (links to VS-103)

steps.activity: Trade Capability/Store-Ops build and maintain the mentor/master-tradesperson network: identify and qualify master tradespersons per trade/store, define mentor role and time commitment, and balance mentor capacity with apprentice cohorts (links to W3817)

Trade Capability/L&D train and certify mentors/coaches (coaching skills, assessment consistency links to W3828), recognize and reward mentor contribution (links to W630, and compensation links to VS-102 where applicable)
Trade Capability manage mentor–apprentice matching, coaching cadence, and mentor feedback into progress tracking (links to W3821); resolve matching/coaching issues

fields.Participants: Trade Capability, HR (links to VS-19/VS-103), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Mentors (links to W3820), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Occupational Health (links to VS-83)

workflows.name: Apprentice Progress Tracking, Feedback & Welfare Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "track apprentice progress against curriculum and competency" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews and feedback" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-issue of "Trade Capability/HR/Occupational-Health manage apprentice welfare" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: early flagging and remediation; operational: welfare management
Pain Points / Risks: - **At-risk-dropout risk**: Struggling apprentice lost; mitigated by early flagging and remediation
- **Welfare risk**: Safety/wellbeing issues unaddressed; mitigated by welfare management
System Touchpoints: - L&D/HRIS (links to VS-103.3/VS-19.4); HR cases (links to VS-103.1); occupational health (links to VS-83); labor relations (links to VS-84); speak-up (links to VS-119)

steps.activity: Trade Capability/L&D track apprentice progress against curriculum and competency (links to W3815/W3819): module completion, practical sign-off, assessment results, attendance, and mentor evaluation; flag at-risk apprentices
Trade Capability/HR run periodic apprentice reviews and feedback: performance feedback, two-way feedback on the program/mentors/stores, and corrective/remediation plans for struggling apprentices

Trade Capability/HR/Occupational-Health manage apprentice welfare: wellbeing, safety incidents (links to W3823), grievances (links to VS-84/VS-119), stipend/allowance issues (links to W3812), and reasonable support

fields.Participants: Trade Capability, HR (links to VS-19.1), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Recruiting (links to VS-19.1), DC Ops (links to VS-04), In-Store Services (links to VS-09), Compensation (links to VS-102)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "track, with mobility" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-599 (ensure controlled execution — Apprenticeship Cohort Operations, Mentorship & Competency Assessment (PA-123.2).)
- operational: placement planning tied to workforce needs; operational: career pathway
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-placement risk**: Certified apprentices not placed → attrition/wasted investment; mitigated by placement planning tied to workforce needs
- **Career-dead-end risk**: No growth path post-certification → attrition; mitigated by career pathway
System Touchpoints: - Recruiting/onboarding (links to VS-19.1); store ops (links to VS-07); mobility (links to W682); compensation (links to VS-102); L&D (links to VS-19.4); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Trade Capability/HR/Store-Ops convert certified apprentices to regular roles: placement into open department-specialist/sales-associate/fabrication/installation roles per capability and store need, with compliant conversion per DOLE rules (links to W3812) and competitive offer (links to VS-102)

Trade Capability/HR/L&D define the trade career pathway: certified apprentice → department specialist → master tradesperson/mentor → supervisor → store-manager-track, with mobility (links to W682/W3779) and continued certification (links to VS-19.4/W1127)
Trade Capability/Analytics track conversion, placement, retention, and career-progression outcomes (links to W3832) and feed insights into cohort planning (links to W3817) and TA (links to VS-121)

fields.Participants: Trade Capability, HSE (links to VS-24), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Occupational Health (links to VS-83), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Mentors (links to W3820)

workflows.name: Apprenticeship Safety, PPE & Trade-Specific HSE Integration

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-assign of "assignment and safe work practices for apprentices, with mentor supervision" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-599 (ensure controlled execution — Apprenticeship Cohort Operations, Mentorship & Competency Assessment (PA-123.2).)
- operational: induction, supervision, PPE; operational: HSE integration
Pain Points / Risks: - **Apprentice-injury risk**: Inexperienced apprentice injured on machinery/chemicals; mitigated by induction, supervision, PPE
- **HSE-non-compliance risk**: Apprentice activity violates HSE rules; mitigated by HSE integration
System Touchpoints: - HSE (links to VS-24); occupational health (links to VS-83); PPE (links to W172); DG/chemical (links to VS-114); incident (links to W140/W861)

steps.activity: Trade Capability/HSE integrate trade-specific safety into the apprenticeship: safety induction (links to VS-24), trade-specific hazard training (saw/cut machinery, electrical safety, chemical/paint handling links to VS-114/W1465 SDS, lifting, working at height for installation), and PPE standards and issuance (links to W172)

Trade Capability/HSE/Store-Ops ensure supervised, age/role-appropriate task assignment and safe work practices for apprentices, with mentor supervision (links to W3820) and incident reporting (links to VS-24/W140)
Trade Capability/Occupational-Health manage apprentice occupational health (links to VS-83), first-aid/clinic access, and any incident/injury follow-up (links to VS-24/W861)

fields.Participants: Trade Capability, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Vendor Mgmt (links to VS-03), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Retail Media (links to VS-48), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Compliance/ABC (links to VS-86.3)
fields.Trigger: Vendor cycle; product launch; sponsorship opportunity

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Trade Capability/Vendor-Mgmt manage vendor sponsorship and funded-training governance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report to merchandising/vendor-scorecard" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-599 (ensure controlled execution — Apprenticeship Cohort Operations, Mentorship & Competency Assessment (PA-123.2).)
- operational: brand-neutrality and balanced curriculum; operational: ABC governance (links to VS-86)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-bias risk**: Vendor training skews apprentice toward sponsored brands; mitigated by brand-neutrality and balanced curriculum
- **ABC risk**: Vendor sponsorship creates undue influence; mitigated by ABC governance (links to VS-86.3)
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising (links to VS-01); vendor (links to VS-03); L&D (links to VS-19.4); retail media (links to VS-48); ABC (links to VS-86.3); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67)

steps.activity: Trade Capability/Merchandising integrate vendor and product training into the apprenticeship: vendor-led product/brand training (power tools, paint, electrical, appliances), new-product-launch familiarization (links to VS-01.1), and category expertise — complementing BuildRight's own curriculum (links to W3810)

Trade Capability/Vendor-Mgmt manage vendor sponsorship and funded-training governance: vendor sponsorship of tools/kits/curriculum, compliant with anti-bribery (links to VS-86.3) and brand-neutrality (no vendor favoritism in selling — links to VS-124), and documented
Trade Capability measure vendor-training effectiveness and apprentice product knowledge (links to W3819/W3832), and report to merchandising/vendor-scorecard (links to VS-67)
